b1-unit-37.37.1 At the auto shop:
Mechanic: Good morning! What can I do for you?
Carol: Hi! My car needs servicing. The last time it was checked was about a year ago, and I'm driving to see a friend in Miami next weekend.
Mechanic: OK. Then we'll do a basic service. I have some free time on Thursday. Can you bring it in at nine?
Carol: Thursday at nine is perfect. But I need it back by Friday morning.
Mechanic: It should be ready by then, unless we need to order new parts. Then it might take longer.
Carol: OK. And I think there's a problem. The oil level keeps dropping, so there might be a leak.
Mechanic: We'll find out what the matter is when you bring it in. If there's a leak, a part probably needs to be replaced.
Carol: Also, the left brake light is broken, and the windshield wipers need changing. They make a horrible noise. Oh, and the battery died twice last month.
Mechanic: The battery might just need recharging, but if it's old, it'll need to be replaced. How old is it?
Carol: I have no idea. I bought the car used three years ago.
Mechanic: Then we'll test it. Do you want us to check the brake pads and the tires too?
Carol: Yes, please. Will that cost extra?
Mechanic: No, you don't need to pay extra for that. It's all part of the service. You only need to pay for new parts.
Carol: Great! The last shop charged me forty dollars just to fill up the windshield washer fluid.
Mechanic: Forty dollars? Wow. Don't worry, you'll get a reasonable price here. See you on Thursday!
